data.text/markdown:
Counties

This notebook accompanies chapter 10 of the monograph Minimum-Distortion Embedding. In this eample notebook, we'll use PyMDE to embed and visualize 3,220 US counties, described by their demographic data (collected between 2013-2017 by an ACS longitudinal survey). We'll then color each county by the fraction of voters who voted for a democratic candidate in the 2016 presidential election. Interestingly, the embedding vaguely resembles a map of the US, though no geographic data was used to compute the embedding.
Below is the raw dataframe, which was preprocessed using the code in scripts/preprocess_counties_data.py. The preprocessed data is stored in dataset.data
We now make a neighbor-preserving embedding, to explore the local relationships in the data.
Finally we visualize the embedding, rotating it so that it vaguely resembles a map of the US. Note that counties that voted Republican tend to cluster together, as do counties that voted Democratic.
